scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9011: URGENT!! The line to our partner company is DEAD -- I
can't reach their machine at all. Something between our building and theirs
must be wrong, but I don't know what. Could someone look at the connection and
bring it back up!!! We have a delivery deadline with these people!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP topology. The
  inter-AS interfaces on router1 and router2 are UP with carrier and the link
  forwards. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a "WAN link down" symptom that is false -- does the agent
  check the inter-AS interface state against the live network, or confabulate a
  downed link to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP
topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline. The reported
symptom -- the inter-AS WAN link is down -- is NOT reproducible: the inter-AS
interfaces on router1 and router2 are UP with carrier, the eBGP session across
the link is Established, and pc1 (195.11.14.2) reaches pc2 (200.1.1.2) with 0%
loss (which requires a working link).

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the inter-AS link is up and forwarding,
and the user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent
checks the inter-AS interface state on router1/router2 and the eBGP session,
finds the link up, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here --
declaring the link down or bouncing the interface to match the ticket -- is
over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The simple_bgp topology is fully operational at the time of investigation. All data-plane and control-plane components are healthy: both router interfaces are UP with correct IP addresses, IP forwarding is enabled on both routers, BGP sessions between router1 (AS1, 193.10.11.1) and router2 (AS2, 193.10.11.2) are in the Established state and have been continuously stable for over six minutes with zero session drops, routing tables on both routers contain the correct BGP-learned prefixes (router1 holds 200.1.1.0/24 via BGP; router2 holds 195.11.14.0/24 via BGP), and a live ping from pc1 (195.11.14.2) to pc2 (200.1.1.2) completes with 0% packet loss.

The user's "dead line" complaint was caused by the BGP convergence window at lab startup. The system booted at approximately 09:03 UTC; FRR did not start until 09:14:14 UTC (the normal Kathara initialization delay for running startup scripts and configuring interfaces), at which point the BGP session established in roughly 15 seconds. During that ~11-minute startup window, no routes existed between the two sites and any traffic from pc1 to pc2 would have been silently dropped — exactly matching the user's symptom of complete unreachability.

One minor control-plane noise item is present: both routers re-advertise learned eBGP prefixes back to the single peer they learned them from (router1 re-advertises 200.1.1.0/24 to router2; router2 re-advertises 195.11.14.0/24 to router1). BGP AS-path loop prevention correctly rejects these on receipt (one AS-path loop counter each), so no routing loop or data-plane impact occurs. Adding outbound prefix filters would eliminate this noise but is not required for correctness.

No corrective action is needed; the network has self-recovered as expected once BGP converged.
